# `Browser.Gamepad.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Gamepad.Internals — the low-level Gamepad port surface: the
closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` request/subscribe
wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.Gamepad` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:gamepad` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.Gamepad` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type.

  * `Watch` — begin a session-stream: connect/disconnect events and polled
    state frames arrive on the inbound subscription. The JS host starts
    polling via `requestAnimationFrame`.
  * `StopWatch` — end the active watch, stopping the `requestAnimationFrame`
    poll loop. A no-op when no watch is active.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — deliberately NOT the app's internal
`Msg`. Every variant the Gamepad API can push is enumerated, so the fold in
the high-level layer is EXHAUSTIVE and an unavailability can never be
silently dropped: it becomes a typed `Err`.

  * `Connected index id` — a gamepad connected (index 0..3, browser-assigned
    id string).
  * `Disconnected index` — a gamepad disconnected.
  * `StateFrame index buttons axes` — a polled state snapshot for one
    connected gamepad. `buttons` is a list of pressed flags (one per
    physical button, in Gamepad API order); `axes` is a list of axis values,
    each in the range -1.0..1.0 (one per physical axis, in Gamepad API
    order).
  * `Unavailable` — the Gamepad API is absent in this context.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink registers the gamepad event listeners and
starts the `requestAnimationFrame` poll; replies arrive inbound as `JsMsg`
frames.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error JsMsg
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot `JsCmd` → `Task Error JsMsg`.
Routes through `Js.request` with the `inbound` decoder so the correlated
reply is decoded fail-closed by the same gate the `subscribe` path uses.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is handed to `toMsg`.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.
